title: Even-harmonic generation through nonequilibrium steady-state symmetry breaking
authors: Milad Jangjan, Arman Kashef, Siamak Pooyan, Stefan Scheel, Dieter Bauer
abstract: High-harmonic generation (HHG) in inversion-symmetric systems is typically restricted to odd harmonics by symmetry. Here, we show that this selection rule can be broken without modifying the underlying Hamiltonian. We investigate a boundary-driven Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain coupled to source and sink reservoirs and demonstrate that dissipative dynamics generates a nonequilibrium steady state carrying a finite DC current. While the SSH Hamiltonian retains inversion symmetry, the current-carrying steady-state density matrix does not, leading to the emergence of even harmonics in the emitted spectrum. Using a correlation-matrix approach based on the Lindblad master equation, we obtain the steady state and calculate the resulting HHG response. We find that the intensity of the even harmonics is directly controlled by the transport current, establishing a link between nonequilibrium charge transport and HHG selection rules. Our results uncover a mechanism for even-harmonic generation that relies solely on nonequilibrium steady-state symmetry breaking and provide a route to probing transport currents through ultrafast nonlinear spectroscopy in centrosymmetric quantum systems.
summary: The paper demonstrates that even harmonics can be generated in inversion-symmetric systems by driving them into a current-carrying, non-equilibrium steady state. This effect arises not from structural symmetry breaking but purely from the dissipative coupling to reservoirs. The intensity of these even harmonics is quantitatively linked to the magnitude of the DC charge transport current.
main_problem: The study investigates how even-harmonic generation (HHG) can occur in systems that possess inversion symmetry at the Hamiltonian level, but are driven into a non-equilibrium steady state by external currents.
main_result: The emergence of even harmonics is shown to be directly controlled by the magnitude of the DC transport current, establishing a clear link between nonequilibrium charge transport and the breaking of HHG selection rules.
method: The analysis employs open quantum system theory using the Lindblad master equation formalism, solved via the single-particle correlation matrix approach for steady-state calculations.
model_or_system: The model is a one-dimensional Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain coupled to source and sink reservoirs, simulating boundary-driven current flow in an open quantum system.
key_observables: High-harmonic generation (HHG) spectrum, steady-state transport current ($J_{dc}$), and the Uhlmann fidelity between time-dependent and steady states.
important_parameters: The strength of the boundary coupling ($\gamma$), which dictates the non-equilibrium nature of the state.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to pairing-free Gaussian states, allowing for the use of correlation matrices derived from the Lindblad master equation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the 1D SSH chain setup with reservoirs and applied fields; they also show time evolution of current under different coupling strengths ($\gamma$) and the resulting HHG response spectrum.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical model (SSH chain in open system), derives the steady-state solution using correlation matrices, analyzes the symmetry breaking mechanism due to dissipation, and finally calculates the observable HHG spectrum linked to the DC current.
why_interesting: This work bridges nonlinear quantum optics (HHG) with non-equilibrium condensed matter physics (current transport in open chains), providing a novel spectroscopic probe for charge dynamics in centrosymmetric materials.
